metadata.name: [GCP Cloud SQL MySQL OTel] Instance restarted or failed over
metadata.description: Alerts when a Cloud SQL for MySQL instance restarted or failed over within the last 15 minutes. That means an automatic failover request was recorded, or a minute with less than 55 seconds of uptime (database/uptime, where 59-61 s is collection jitter) was followed by a full minute, so the instance went down and came back. A short-uptime minute is treated as planned and ignored when the instance reported MAINTENANCE in that minute or the minute before or after it. Any other short-uptime minute alerts, including a crash before, after or between maintenance periods in the same window. Ongoing outages are covered by the 'Instance not serving' rule. The alert stays active while the event is inside the window, then recovers. The 15-minute window and 5-minute schedule make sure each event is evaluated at least once, despite the 3-5 minute delivery delay.

query.base:
TS metrics-gcp.cloudsql_mysql.otel-*
| WHERE resource.attributes.gcp.resource_type == "cloudsql_database"
// Per instance and minute: seconds of uptime (about 60 when up the whole minute), auto-failover requests,
// whether the instance was in MAINTENANCE, and the MySQL marker. MIN/MAX collapse duplicate points.
| STATS uptime_s = MIN(MIN_OVER_TIME(`metrics.cloudsql.googleapis.com/database/uptime`)),
        failovers = MAX(MAX_OVER_TIME(`metrics.cloudsql.googleapis.com/database/auto_failover_request_count`)),
        maintenance = MAX(MAX_OVER_TIME(`metrics.cloudsql.googleapis.com/database/instance_state`)) WHERE state == "MAINTENANCE",
        marker = SUM(COUNT_OVER_TIME(`metrics.cloudsql.googleapis.com/database/mysql/queries`))
  BY `@timestamp` = TBUCKET(1 minute), database_id
// uptime and instance_state are sampled separately, so a MAINTENANCE minute also covers the minute before and after it.
// Copy each MAINTENANCE minute to its neighbours and regroup, so every minute knows whether maintenance was near.
| EVAL minute = CASE(maintenance == 1, MV_APPEND(MV_APPEND(`@timestamp` - 1 minute, `@timestamp`), `@timestamp` + 1 minute), `@timestamp`)
| MV_EXPAND minute
| STATS uptime_s = MIN(uptime_s) WHERE minute == `@timestamp`,
        failovers = MAX(failovers) WHERE minute == `@timestamp`,
        marker = SUM(marker) WHERE minute == `@timestamp`,
        near_maintenance = MAX(maintenance)
  BY minute, database_id
// Short-uptime minutes, and those not near a MAINTENANCE minute (unplanned)
| STATS partial_uptime_minutes = COUNT(uptime_s) WHERE uptime_s > 0 AND uptime_s < 55,
        zero_uptime_minutes = COUNT(uptime_s) WHERE uptime_s == 0,
        unplanned_short_minutes = COUNT(uptime_s) WHERE uptime_s < 55 AND COALESCE(near_maintenance, 0) == 0,
        latest_uptime_s = LAST(uptime_s, CASE(uptime_s IS NOT NULL, minute, NULL)),
        failover_requests = SUM(failovers),
        marker = SUM(marker)
  BY database_id

data.content:
## Cloud SQL MySQL instance restarted or failed over

The instance had downtime and is serving again. `event_type` is `auto failover` when Cloud SQL recorded an automatic failover request (HA instances), otherwise `restart`. `zero_uptime_minutes` and `partial_uptime_minutes` show how long it was down, and `unplanned_short_minutes` how many of those minutes were not near maintenance.

### Triage
1. Open **[GCP OTel] Cloud SQL MySQL Instance Detail**. Check *Lowest uptime per minute* for the restart and *Memory usage vs quota* just before it: memory climbing to the quota points to an out-of-memory restart.
2. Check the Cloud SQL error log and operations list in the Google Cloud console for a crash, OOM kill, flag change, tier change or failover.
3. After a failover, the standby is rebuilt, and the instance runs without HA protection until `available_for_failover` returns above 0.
4. Expect a cold InnoDB buffer pool after a restart: a lower buffer pool hit ratio, more disk reads and slower queries for a while.
5. Check the clients for a reconnect storm (*Connections near the max_connections limit*, *Failed connection surge*).

### Common causes
Out-of-memory (too many connections or an oversized buffer pool for the tier), a MySQL crash, an instance or flag change that needs a restart, a zonal failure that triggers an HA failover.

### Tuning
Replace `unplanned_short_minutes > 0` with `partial_uptime_minutes + zero_uptime_minutes > 0` to also alert on restarts during maintenance. Restarts and failovers are always worth recording, so suppress notifications instead of raising thresholds.
